episodes.title: Security Saves Kathryn Krick From a Demon Attack
episodes.description:
At Ignite Revival Paris, Kathryn Krick attempts to cast demons out of a woman who becomes increasingly aggressive while security intervenes to keep her away from Krick. Krick repeatedly commands spirits to leave in Jesus’ name, but the confrontation does not end with the immediate deliverance seen in the biblical accounts examined in this video.

The footage raises a serious question about Krick’s claim to apostolic authority and spiritual power. While Krick continues commanding the spirits, the woman resists and the situation becomes increasingly physical. Security has to step in and remain between the woman and Krick, while Krick eventually steps away and says that the woman needs to renounce certain things before deliverance can take place.

The video compares this encounter with Acts 16:18, where Paul commands the spirit of divination to leave the slave girl and Scripture says that it left at that very moment. The question is whether the kind of prolonged, unsuccessful deliverance seen here is consistent with the authority and instantaneous deliverances associated with the apostles in Scripture.

episodes.title: TikToker Makes a Fool of Kathryn Krick
episodes.description:
A TikToker deliberately pretended to be possessed by a demon at Kathryn Krick’s deliverance event—and Krick treated the performance as a genuine manifestation. Elena went to the event specifically to troll Krick, put on an elaborate display, and see whether the self-proclaimed deliverance minister could tell that she was acting.

During the encounter, Elena screamed, flailed, kicked, and pretended to be delivered from demons while Kathryn Krick commanded the supposed spirits to leave in Jesus’ name. Elena later explained exactly what she had done, making it clear that she was not actually experiencing the demonic manifestation Krick was responding to. The incident therefore raises a straightforward question about Krick’s claimed ability to discern demonic activity: if someone deliberately pretends to be possessed, can she tell the difference between an act and a genuine manifestation?

The video also examines what happened to the footage afterward. Elena says that after recording the livestream, she discovered that her appearance had been cut from the uploaded footage. Meanwhile, footage of another man attempting a similar stunt remained because, unlike Elena, his performance was recognized and confronted. This creates an important contrast between the footage that made Krick look good and the footage that did not.

I examine Elena’s account, the available footage, Kathryn Krick’s response, and what this incident demonstrates about her deliverance ministry and claims of spiritual discernment. The issue is not whether Elena’s trolling was appropriate or whether she is a Christian—she explicitly says she is not. The question is whether a person claiming to identify and cast out demons can distinguish genuine spiritual manifestations from someone deliberately putting on a performance.
